title: Number of Islands
statement: A grid of '1' (land) and '0' (water) is given as a list of strings. Return the number of islands. An island is a 4-directionally connected group of land cells.
hints: Every unvisited land cell starts a new island.
DFS or BFS floods the whole island and marks it visited so it is not counted again.
Mutating the grid to water is a valid visited mark when the caller does not need the original grid.

approaches.name: DFS flood
approaches.explanation: The recursion or an explicit stack marks the component.

editorial: Scan every cell. When you see land, increment the island count and flood-fill every land cell reachable in four directions. Mark visited cells as water so later scans skip them. Each cell is entered a constant number of times, so the algorithm is linear in the number of cells.
